Two designated off-leash beaches (Hobie Island on the Rickenbacker Causeway and Haulover Dog Beach in Sunny Isles) plus large fenced dog parks at South Pointe, Margaret Pace, Tropical Park and Amelia Earhart give travellers genuine off-leash options. The Brightline intercity rail accepts pets up to 25 lb on every train, MIA airport is a CDC-approved dog-import gateway with two indoor pet relief areas, the Metromover and Metrobus admit small pets in carriers, and 24/7 emergency vet care is available across the metro. Peak season runs November to April; May to October brings 50-55 °C asphalt heat that limits midday walking.

name: Milan
intro: Milan is Italy's style capital and increasingly one of its most pet-welcoming cities: boutique hotels in the Navigli and Brera districts actively court guests with dogs. Parco Sempione, a 47-hectare green lung right beside the Castello Sforzesco, is perfect for morning walks before a day of exploring.

name: Modena
intro: Emilia-Romagna's gastronomic heart and home of balsamic vinegar, Ferrari, Maserati, Pavarotti. The Cathedral, Ghirlandina tower and Piazza Grande form a UNESCO World Heritage trio (1997). Compact and flat, easy walking with a dog. 35 min from Bologna and 1h45 from Milan by train. Spring and autumn are ideal; summers are humid (32°C), winters foggy.

name: Mojácar
intro: Mojácar pairs a whitewashed hilltop pueblo with around 7 km of Costa de Almería seafront and a long, flat Paseo Marítimo that is ideal for dog walks. In 2025 it opened its first official dog beach, the Playa del Perulejo near the Macenas watchtower, making it an easy long-stay summer base for pet owners.

name: Montpellier
intro: Montpellier's sun-soaked terraces, tram-laced streets, and the Grand Travers beach nearby make it one of southern France's most pet-welcoming cities for a city break.

name: Montréal
intro: Montréal is one of the very few North American cities where a full-size dog can legally ride the subway, and it pairs that with 65 fenced dog runs, 14 km of car-free canal path and a terrasse culture that runs from May to October.

name: Montreux
intro: Montreux on the Swiss Riviera blends Lake Geneva palms, the Château de Chillon, the Lavaux UNESCO vineyards, and the Quais Fleuris promenade where leashed dogs are welcome from Vevey to Villeneuve.

name: Munich
intro: Munich's English Garden, beer garden culture (dogs welcome), and excellent hotels make it ideal for a city break with your pet.

name: Nantes
intro: France’s most liveable city has ten dog parks (caniparcs), a QUALIDOG restaurant network, and a 12 km dog-friendly cultural trail, making it one of the most welcoming destinations in Europe for travelling with a pet.

name: Naples
intro: Italy's chaotic, passionate southern capital, gateway to Pompeii, Vesuvius, Capri and the Amalfi Coast. Dense historic-centre alleys, seafront Lungomare, 134 hectares of Bosco di Capodimonte, and pet-welcoming trattorie make it a rewarding (if demanding) stop for dog owners.

name: Narbonne
intro: Narbonne is a 55 000-resident Languedoc-Roussillon city with the unfinished Gothic Cathédrale Saint-Just, the Via Domitia Roman road, the UNESCO Canal de la Robine through the historic centre, Les Halles covered market, the 17 000-hectare Massif de la Clape garrigue, and a 15 km Mediterranean sand corridor 15 minutes east anchored by the year-round off-leash Saint-Pierre-la-Mer plage canine at Fleury-d'Aude (postal 11560).

name: Naxos
intro: Naxos is the green, laid-back giant of the Cyclades, where the giant marble Portara gateway frames the sunset over a whitewashed old town and the longest sandy beaches in the islands stretch south toward Plaka. It is one of the most relaxed Greek islands for travelling with a dog, with open beaches, walkable Venetian lanes, and cool inland marble villages.

name: Nazaré
intro: Nazaré, Portugal's Atlantic fishing town turned big-wave capital, pairs the clifftop Sítio quarter and Forte de São Miguel Arcanjo with the world-famous Praia do Norte canyon swells, a vintage funicular linking upper and lower town, and a long sandy beach where dogs are welcome outside the lifeguarded zone in summer.

name: Neringa
intro: Neringa is the UNESCO Curonian Spit resort municipality of four small lagoon villages (Nida, Juodkrante, Preila, Pervalka) on a 52 km sand spit reached only by ferry from Klaipeda, where leashed dogs roam pine-forest trails, the Parnidis sundial dune and the Nida lagoon promenade.

name: Nerja
intro: Nerja is a whitewashed Costa del Sol town on the Málaga coast, famous for the Balcón de Europa promontory, the prehistoric Nerja Caves and golden beaches like Burriana and Carabeo. With leashed dogs welcome on its terraces and promenade, two new fenced dog parks and the cool Río Chíllar river walk, it makes an easy summer base for pet owners.

name: New York
intro: The first US destination on the site: Manhattan's skyline, 70+ dog runs, 24/7 emergency vets, and the most generous urban off-leash hours in America (5–9 am, 9 pm–1 am in Central and Prospect Parks). Dense, demanding in summer heat, and rewarding for travellers who want a pet-friendly city break beyond Europe.

name: Newquay
intro: A north Cornwall surf town wrapped in beaches, where most of the sand stays dog-friendly all year and dogs share the coast path, the harbour boat trips and the harbour pubs. The one summer restriction to know is Porth Beach, which bans dogs 10am-6pm from 1 July to 31 August, while Fistral, Crantock and Watergate Bay welcome dogs year-round.

name: Nice
intro: Nice's Mediterranean climate, Promenade des Anglais, and abundance of terrace restaurants make it a superb destination for pets year-round.

name: Nîmes
intro: Nîmes is the third corner of the Provence Roman triangle (with Avignon and Arles): the best-preserved Roman amphitheatre in the world, the UNESCO Maison Carrée, the 15-hectare Jardins de la Fontaine and the Pont du Gard 25 km north. The Arènes carry the Qualidog label and admit leashed dogs of all sizes free of charge, a French rarity.

name: Nuremberg
intro: Bavaria's second city and one of medieval Europe's great free imperial centres. The Kaiserburg castle, half-timbered Altstadt, and Albrecht Dürer's house anchor a compact UNESCO Tentative-listed core. Famous for its Christkindlesmarkt (Christmas market, since 1628), Lebkuchen gingerbread and Rostbratwurst. 1h05 from Munich and 4h from Berlin by ICE. Spring and autumn are ideal; winters cold but festive.

name: Olbia
intro: Olbia is the lively gateway to Sardinia's Costa Smeralda, where a walkable granite old town meets the turquoise Gulf of Olbia. With a designated dog beach at Le Saline and dog-friendly terraces along Corso Umberto, it makes an easy, sun-soaked base for a pet-friendly summer on the island.

name: Olhão
intro: Olhão, the Algarve's most authentic working fishing port, pairs a cubist whitewashed old town and the famous 1916 red-brick waterfront markets with direct ferries into the Parque Natural da Ria Formosa and its barrier islands of Armona, Culatra and Farol. Municipal dog parks, flat waterfront gardens and near-empty island beaches from October to May make it a natural base for travelling with a dog, with Faro airport only 15 minutes away.

name: Olomouc
intro: Moravia's baroque secret is everything over-touristed Europe is not: UNESCO monuments without queues, a green belt of rampart parks around the old town, forest trails up the Svatý Kopeček pilgrimage hill, two vet clinics with round-the-clock emergency cover, and a genuine rarity, a zoo that admits leashed, muzzled dogs for a 100 CZK ticket.

name: Opatija
intro: Opatija is the grande dame of the Croatian Riviera, where leashed dogs walk the 12 km Lungomare seafront, cool off at two designated dog beaches, and hike the Ucka nature park above the Belle Epoque villas.

name: Oropesa del Mar
intro: Oropesa del Mar is a Mediterranean beach town on the Costa del Azahar between Valencia and Castellón, with a 15th-century hilltop castle, a working fishing port, and kilometres of sandy beach open to dogs outside peak season. The Serra d'Irta Natural Park to the south offers the last undeveloped stretch of Valencia coast.

name: Osaka
intro: Osaka, the buzzing commercial heart of the Kansai region, is a workable but rule-bound city for dog owners: as elsewhere in Japan, dogs ride JR West, the Osaka Metro and city buses only inside a closed carrier, and most indoor restaurants exclude them, so the pleasure lies outdoors. Leashed dogs are welcome on the outer paths and lawns of Osaka Castle Park (though not inside the castle keep or museum), along the Dotonbori canal-side and in the riverside greenery of Nakanoshima and Utsubo parks. Pet taxis cover larger dogs, international sitter platforms have Osaka listings, and the Shinkansen puts Kyoto around 15 minutes away and Tokyo about 2 hours 30 minutes away for a wider Japan trip.

name: Oslo
intro: Oslo sits at the intersection of city life and wild nature, making it arguably Scandinavia's best city for dogs: fjords, forests, and snow-covered trails are all reachable by public transport. Hotels here routinely provide dog beds and bowls, and the expansive Nordmarka forest starts just 20 minutes from the centre.

name: Ostend
intro: Ostend, the Belgian Royal Resort on the North Sea with 9 km of sandy promenade, year-round dog-beach zones at Mariakerke, Raversijde and Oosteroever, the Kusttram (longest tram line in the world, 67 km) and the Stena Line ferry to Ramsgate (UK), is one of the easiest pet-travel hubs on the Belgian coast.

name: Oviedo
intro: The pre-Romanesque UNESCO capital of green-Spain Asturias pairs the dog-friendly cider terraces of Calle Gascona, the Bulevar de la Sidra, with the panoramic Monte Naranco hill trails, a central Campo de San Francisco park, a 24/7 veterinary hospital in Buenavista, and an easy FEVE rail link to the Asturias coast and Picos de Europa, one of the most relaxed northern-Spanish cities for a dog-inclusive trip.

name: Oxford
intro: England's medieval university city, honey-coloured college quadrangles, the 162-hectare off-lead Port Meadow, the Christ Church Meadow loop and the Thames towpath. Compact, walkable, with one of the country's highest pub dog-welcome rates and 24/7 emergency vet cover at Medivet Woodstock.

name: Padstow
intro: A pretty fishing harbour on the Camel estuary in north Cornwall, and one of the county's easiest dog holidays. Dogs share the quayside pubs, the flat Camel Trail and the estuary beaches, with Harbour Cove and Daymer Bay staying dog-friendly all year; the summer bans to know are Trevone (no dogs 15 May to 30 September, 10am to 6pm) and St George's Cove (1 July to 31 August).

name: Padua
intro: Veneto's UNESCO-listed university city, anchored by Europe's largest square Prato della Valle (88,620 m²), 25+ km of porticoed arcades, off-leash aree cani in every district and a fixed €5 Trenitalia fare to Venice or Verona in under 40 minutes. Compact, walkable and one of Italy's quietest dog-friendly cultural bases.

name: Palamós
intro: Palamós is a 17,000-resident Costa Brava centre fishing-port municipality in the Baix Empordà comarca of Girona, defined by its active Port de Palamós fleet (3rd by volume in Catalonia), the Llotja de Palamós afternoon fish auction, the Museu de la Pesca on the harbour, the casc antic of Sant Joan de Palamós on the hilltop, the free open-air ruins of the Castell de Sant Esteve de Mar on the clifftop north, and a four-port coastline from the 1 km Platja Gran (town centre) to the fjord-like La Fosca, the postcard fishermen-hut cove of Cala S'Alguer, the Platja del Castell (year-round dog-beach zone on the northern section) and the southern Cala Margarida. The Gamba de Palamós PDO red prawn and the Cuina del Peix de Palamós Slow-Food programme define the village kitchen. The 6 km Camí de Ronda GR-92 clifftop coastal path links Palamós north to Calella de Palafrugell. No train station; access by Moventis bus from Girona (1 h 30) or by car on the C-31 from the AP-7 motorway. The reference 24/7 emergency vet is the Hospital Veterinari Costa Brava in Palafrugell, 5 km north.

name: Palermo
intro: Sicily's vibrant capital (~660k inhabitants), gateway to Sicilian beaches and the Mediterranean's chaotic-baroque heart. The Arab-Norman UNESCO ensemble (Cathedral, Royal Palace's Capella Palatina, Zisa) layers nine centuries of Mediterranean rule. Vucciria + Ballarò markets, the Foro Italico seafront, Mondello dog-beach 11 km north. 1h flight from Rome, ferry hub to Tunis and Naples. Sicilian taverna culture is unusually dog-friendly on terraces.

name: Pamplona
intro: Capital of Navarra in Northern Spain, Hemingway's favourite city, world-famous for the San Fermines bull-running festival (6-14 July). ~205k inhabitants, walled medieval old town, the Citadel park (Ciudadela, 280k m²), and the Camino de Santiago French route runs straight through the centre. 1h45 from Madrid by Renfe AVE, 1h from Bilbao by Alsa bus. One of Spain's most dog-positive cities, pintxo bar culture welcomes dogs on terraces year-round.

name: Paphos
intro: Paphos pairs UNESCO-listed antiquity with a sun-soaked coastline, where a renovated seafront broadwalk links the harbour castle to the Tombs of the Kings. Mild winters and a long, dog-walkable promenade make it a rewarding year-round and summer destination with a pet, provided you manage the Cyprus heat.

name: Paris
intro: Paris welcomes pets in many hotels, cafés, and even some restaurants.

name: Pärnu
intro: Estonia's summer capital pairs a pastel wooden old town with a huge sandy bay, and treats dogs remarkably well: four official dog swimming spots (river mole, Mai, Vana-Pärnu and Raeküla), a fenced double dog park with agility gear near Mai beach, a boardwalk through the Rannaniit coastal meadow reserve, and a tourist board that publishes its own list of dog-friendly cafes and spa hotels.

name: Paros
intro: Paros is one of the most relaxed Cyclades islands for dog owners, pairing the Venetian-flavoured fishing harbour of Naoussa and the old-town lanes of Parikia with informal dog-welcoming coves and shaded marble trails. The real planning is around the summer heat and the muzzle-and-cabin ferry rules that bring you to the island.

name: Peniche
intro: Peniche is a working fishing port on a peninsula jutting into the Atlantic, 90 km north of Lisbon. A 16th-century fortress, the world-class surf breaks of Baleal, dramatic cliff paths circling the cape, and a local culture shaped entirely by the sea make it one of Portugal's most atmospheric and dog-friendly coastal towns.

name: Perpignan
intro: Perpignan, the sunny Catalan capital of the French south, is a compact and genuinely dog-friendly city with around 37 marked dog areas, a tolerant terrace culture, a 24-hour emergency vet, and easy access to the dog-friendly Roussillon beaches of Canet-en-Roussillon and Torreilles.

name: Perugia
intro: Umbria's hilltop capital pairs Etruscan gates and medieval lanes with a surprisingly practical dog setup: a 24/7 university veterinary hospital, fenced dog runs at Pian di Massiano, a monorail that carries small dogs free, panoramic gardens for sunset walks, and Lake Trasimeno's dog beaches 30 minutes away. In July, Umbria Jazz turns the whole acropolis into an open-air stage.

name: Piran
intro: Piran, Slovenia's Venetian jewel on the Adriatic Riviera, packs Tartini Square, the San Giorgio bell tower, the medieval Walls of Piran and a car-free old town into a stone peninsula ringed by pet-friendly seafront terraces, with Monty's Dog Beach at Lucija, the Strunjan flysch cliffs and the Sečovlje salt pans within easy reach.

name: Pisa
intro: Pisa pairs a compact UNESCO Old Town with the 23,000-hectare Migliarino San Rossore park and the dog-friendly Tyrrhenian coast at Marina di Pisa, all reachable by city bus. The University Veterinary Hospital adds a 24-hour safety net.

name: Portimão
intro: Portimão is a lively Algarve port city wrapped around the Arade river, best known for its golden Praia da Rocha resort beneath dramatic red cliffs. With a long seafront boardwalk, a busy marina and the Ria de Alvor estuary boardwalk nearby, it makes an easy, walkable summer base for travellers with dogs, as long as you plan around the heat and the seasonal beach bans.

name: Porto
intro: Porto's hilly streets, river esplanades, and laid-back attitude make it one of Portugal's most welcoming cities for travelling with a dog.

name: Poznan
intro: Poznan is the cradle of the Polish state, founded in 966 around the Cathedral Island where the first Polish king Mieszko I was baptised. The colourful Stary Rynek (Old Market Square) is one of the largest medieval squares in Europe, with the famous mechanical goats butting heads on the Town Hall at noon. Beyond the centre, the 64-hectare Lake Malta with its city beach, the Citadel Park's panoramic terrace, and the Wielkopolska National Park 30 km south make Poznan a quiet pet-travel favourite. Trams accept dogs with a single ticket, around forty fenced off-leash zones are scattered across the city, and the cafe terraces around the Rynek welcome leashed dogs without fuss.

name: Prague
intro: Prague's compact old town and riverside parks make it an underrated gem for travelling with dogs.

name: Pula
intro: Istria`s 53,000-resident former Roman capital on the southern tip of the peninsula, anchored by the 1st-century Arena (one of the six best-preserved Roman amphitheatres in the world), the Forum with its Augustan Temple of Augustus, the Arch of the Sergii and the Kaštel fortress hilltop, with the Punta Verudela peninsula 4 km south and the off-leash Cape Kamenjak nature park 10 km further on, plus PUY airport 7 km out, a regional rail link to Slovenia and the seasonal Venezia Lines catamaran to Italy.

name: Quiberon
intro: Quiberon is a wind-swept Breton peninsula town famous for its wild Cote Sauvage cliffs, its long sheltered Grande Plage and its ferries to Belle-Ile. With a cool Atlantic summer, miles of leashed coastal walking on the GR34 and year-round dog beaches, it is one of France's best cool-weather seaside escapes with a dog.

name: Quimper
intro: Quimper is the historic capital of Cornouaille in Finistere, a compact and walkable Breton city of half-timbered houses, the twin-spired Saint-Corentin cathedral and the riverside quays of the Odet. With its cool oceanic summers, riverside walks and easy access to the Cornouaille coast, it makes a relaxed warm-weather base for travellers with a dog.

name: Ras Al Khaimah
intro: Ras Al Khaimah is the United Arab Emirates` quiet outlier for pet travel: a beach-and-mountain resort emirate that, thanks to its official Ras Al-K9 program, is the most dog-welcoming corner of the country. Long natural beaches and the Al Marjan Island corniche meet Jebel Jais, the UAE`s highest peak, with leashed mountain trails and wadi walks behind it. A small set of pet-friendly resorts, cafes and beaches, real local vets led by a 24-hour line, and pet boarding back it up. It is quieter and cheaper than Dubai (45 to 75 minutes south) under the same winter sun, with November to March the comfortable season and strict UAE leash and import rules to plan around.

name: Ravenna
intro: Ravenna pairs UNESCO Byzantine mosaics with flat, walkable streets and a ring of pinewoods and Adriatic lidi on its doorstep. It is an easy, dog-friendly base where leashed walks, dog beaches and relaxed osterie terraces are never far away.

name: Regensburg
intro: A 155,000-resident Bavarian city on the Danube where one of Europe's best-preserved medieval Altstadts (UNESCO since 2006) is fully walkable in 30 minutes with a dog. The 12th-century Steinerne Brücke, the Gothic cathedral of St Peter, the riverside Spitalgarten beer garden and the Walhalla terraces above the Danube anchor a calm, dog-tolerant atmosphere far less crowded than Munich or Nuremberg.

name: Reims
intro: Reims, the coronation city of French kings and the capital of Champagne, combines the UNESCO Notre-Dame Cathedral (33 kings crowned), the Palais du Tau, the Pommery cellar gardens, and direct TGV access from Paris Gare de l'Est in 45 minutes.

name: Rennes
intro: Rennes, capital of Brittany, blends the half-timbered medieval centre rebuilt after the 1720 fire, the 10-hectare Parc du Thabor, France's second-largest Saturday market on Place des Lices, and day-trip access to Saint-Malo and the Côte d'Émeraude, making it one of north-west France's most walkable pet-friendly bases.

name: Rethymno
intro: Rethymno is Crete's most atmospheric old town, where a Venetian harbour, the hilltop Fortezza fortress and a long sandy town beach sit within an easy leashed walk of each other. Its shaded Renaissance alleys and breezy seafront make it a relaxed, dog-friendly base for a summer 2026 escape, best enjoyed in the cooler morning and evening hours.

name: Reykjavik
intro: Reykjavik's clean air, dramatic landscapes, and dog-welcoming culture make it a unique and increasingly popular destination for adventurous pet owners.

name: Rhodes
intro: Rhodes pairs a car-free medieval Old Town and a breezy seafront promenade with quiet, dog-welcoming coves and the shaded streams of historic Rodini Park. It is a relaxed, outdoors-first island for dog owners, where the real planning is around summer heat and the muzzle-and-leash ferry and beach rules.

name: Riga
intro: Riga's Art Nouveau architecture, riverside parks, and affordable hotels make it an emerging gem for pet-friendly city breaks in the Baltics.

name: Rimini
intro: Rimini is the capital of Italy's Adriatic Riviera and one of the country's best beach destinations for dog owners, home to Rimini Dog No Problem (the largest dedicated dog beach on the Emilia-Romagna coast), a fenced off-leash park along the Marecchia river, two 24-hour vets, and a Roman and Renaissance old town that is easy to explore on a leash.

name: Riva del Garda
intro: Riva del Garda sits at the windswept northern tip of Lake Garda in Trentino, where Alpine peaks plunge to a Mediterranean lakeshore. With its arcaded old town, the Ponale cliff path and constant breeze, it is one of Italy's most dog-friendly outdoor bases for a summer lake escape.

name: Rome
intro: Rome combines ancient grandeur with a surprisingly relaxed attitude toward pets: dogs are welcome in many piazzas, parks, and hotel terraces.

name: Roses
intro: Roses is a 20,000-resident Costa Brava nord fishing port and beach town wrapped around the Renaissance Ciutadella de Roses, a 16th-century fortified pentagonal enclosure built under Carlos V on the site of the ancient Greek colony of Rhode (8th century BC) and the Roman Rhodes, with the 12 km crescent of the Bahía de Roses opening south to L`Escala and the Cap de Creus Natural Park headland rising to the north. The 3 km sand Platja de Roses fronts the Passeig Marítim, and a string of dramatic coves wraps north along the Cap de Creus side (Cala Canyelles Petites, Cala Murtra, Cala Calís, Cala Montjoi - site of the legendary El Bulli restaurant 1962-2011 - Cala Joncols, Cala Rostella, Cala Pelosa, Cala Nans, L`Almadrava). Two further heritage anchors complete the picture: the 17th-century star-shaped Castell de la Trinitat on the Punta Falconera headland, and the Dolmen de la Creu d`en Cobertella inland, the largest dolmen in Catalonia (ca. 3000 BC). There is no train station; access is by Moventis bus from Figueres (30 min) or Cadaqués (30 min), or by car on the C-260 or AP-7 motorway. Two town vets refer overnight emergencies to the Hospital Veterinari Empordà in Figueres 18 km west.

name: Rotterdam
intro: Rotterdam is one of Europe's most dog-friendly cities, with free public transport for pets, five off-leash parks, and a vibrant café culture that welcomes dogs by default.

name: Rouen
intro: Rouen, Normandy's Gothic capital on the Seine, combines a medieval old town with the towering Cathédrale Notre-Dame, the iconic Gros Horloge astronomical clock, the Place du Vieux-Marché where Joan of Arc was burned, and easy access to the Côte d'Albâtre beaches at Étretat and Dieppe.

name: Rovinj
intro: Istria`s Venetian jewel on the Adriatic west coast, a former islet of pastel houses tumbling down to the harbour under the 60 m belltower of sv. Eufemije, with the 300-acre Punta Corrente forest park and four signposted dog beaches (Plaža Cisterna at Lone Bay, Plaža Borik, Plaža Mulini, Plaža Škaraba), a bilingual Croatian-Italian Stari Grad, the seasonal Venezia Lines catamaran to Venezia, and one of the most genuinely pet-friendly small towns on the eastern Adriatic.

name: Rügen
intro: Germany's largest island is a Baltic paradise for dogs: official Hundestrand sections in Binz, Sellin and Baabe, the chalk cliffs of Jasmund National Park with leash-friendly beech-forest trails, the Hochuferweg clifftop path to the Granitz hunting lodge, and a steam railway that welcomes four-legged passengers, with nearly the entire coastline opening to dogs from October to April.

name: Saint-Jean-de-Luz
intro: Saint-Jean-de-Luz is a postcard Basque resort on the southwest Atlantic coast, where a calm, swimmable bay sheltered by three sea walls sits below a pedestrian old town of red-shuttered houses. It makes a relaxed long-stay summer base for dog owners who plan around one firm local rule: dogs are banned from every town beach all year, so the walking, dining and coastal-path days do the heavy lifting.

name: Saint-Malo
intro: Saint-Malo is a walled corsair city on Brittany's Emerald Coast where granite ramparts circle a tidal old town facing the Atlantic. With cool summers, a 2 km dog-walkable rampart loop and miles of coastal path, it is one of France's most rewarding cool-weather dog destinations.

name: Saint-Tropez
intro: Saint-Tropez is a 4,000-resident Provençal harbour town on the western Côte d'Azur, defined by its working Vieux Port, the 16th-century Citadelle, the plane-tree-shaded Place des Lices market (Tuesday and Saturday), the 5 km Pampelonne beach sweep in neighbouring Ramatuelle, and the 35 km Sentier du Littoral coastal path around the peninsula. The town has no SNCF station: the nearest rail head is Saint-Raphaël-Valescure 45 km away, linked year-round by Var-Lib bus 7601 (90 min) or seasonally by Bateaux de Saint-Raphaël ferry (50 min); the Bateaux Verts crossing from Sainte-Maxime takes 15 minutes. The two regional airports are Toulon-Hyères (TLN, 1 h) and Nice Côte d'Azur (NCE, 1 h 15). Beach access for dogs runs October to mid-May; rosé-fuelled terrace dining is reliable from May to October.

name: Salamanca
intro: Castile's golden sandstone university city, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988. Compact and walkable: the Plaza Mayor (one of Spain's finest), the twin cathedrals, and the Roman Bridge over the Tormes river. 1.5h by AVE from Madrid. Dogs roam easily through arcaded streets and the Salas Bajas riverside parks. Spring and autumn are ideal; summer hits 35°C, winter brings cold dry nights.

name: Salcombe
intro: A sheltered South Devon sailing town at the mouth of the Kingsbridge estuary, where dogs share the waterside pubs, the National Trust coast paths and the little ferries year-round. The beach dog rules are seasonal: South Sands bans dogs completely from 1 May to 30 September, while North Sands and Mill Bay stay dog-friendly all year. There is no railway station, so most visitors arrive via Totnes and the Tally Ho 164 bus.

name: Salzburg
intro: Salzburg's compact baroque centre and the dramatic Alpine scenery surrounding it create an unforgettable backdrop for travelling with pets. The Mirabell Gardens and the footpaths ascending to the Hohensalzburg fortress are both dog-friendly, and hotels here often provide pet amenities.

name: San Francisco
intro: San Francisco is the cool, foggy Pacific gateway to the Bay Area, where ~30 fenced Rec & Park Dog Play Areas plus the federal GGNRA off-leash sections (Crissy Field East Beach with the Golden Gate Bridge view, Fort Funston bluffs and beach, Ocean Beach north of Stairwell 21) make it one of the densest off-leash networks in the US. Golden Gate Park's Hellman Hollow and Speedway Meadow DPAs anchor the 412-hectare flagship park, Lands End coastal trail leads to the Sutro Baths ruins, and the Presidio's forest paths overlook the Bay. BART, Muni Metro/bus and cable car all accept small pets in carriers free; the Golden Gate Ferry to Sausalito takes leashed dogs free on the outer deck; SFO is a CDC-approved international dog-arrival airport with indoor pet relief areas. Three 24/7 emergency vets (SAGE Mission, SFAMC Fillmore, VEG Greenbrae) cover the metro. Cool fog summers (10-15 °C) and dry sunny fall make it walkable year-round; the only constraints are the hilly streets and the cold Pacific rip currents on the ocean side.

name: San Sebastián
intro: San Sebastián (Donostia) has more registered dogs per inhabitant than any other major Spanish city, and it shows, Michelin-starred restaurants welcome dogs without hesitation, Monte Urgull offers vast off-leash hillside walks, and La Concha's crescent beach opens to dogs every October for a full six months.

name: Sankt Pölten
intro: Lower Austria's quiet capital, a 56,000-resident city on the Traisen river with a pedestrian Baroque Altstadt, the modernist Government Quarter and Klangturm tower, and the Wachau wine villages of Dürnstein, Spitz and Krems all within 45 minutes. Vienna is 25 minutes by Railjet.

name: Sanremo
intro: Sanremo is an easygoing Italian Riviera base with a dog, thanks to its flat seafront, one of Italy's mildest climates, and the long, level Pista Ciclabile coastal path on the former Genoa-Ventimiglia railway. Add the palm-lined Corso Imperatrice, the medieval La Pigna old town, a designated dog-friendly beach, and a 24-hour emergency vet.

name: Sant Antoni de Portmany
intro: The 28,000-resident western capital of Ibiza, world-famous for the Sunset Strip clifftop bars and the Cafe del Mar mixtape tradition since 1980, the 14th-century Església de Sant Antoni de Portmany (the oldest church on Ibiza), Hostal La Torre and Punta Galera for quieter sunsets, white-sand Cala Bassa, sunset-facing Cala Conta and family-friendly Cala Tarida on the west coast, Es Vedrà boat excursions, and a Baleària fast ferry from the Port Deportiu to Dénia on the Spanish mainland (2h45) with pet cabins on the Eleanor Roosevelt. Ibiza Airport (IBZ) 15 km south-east by taxi or TIB L8 bus.

name: Sant Josep de sa Talaia
intro: Largest municipality on Ibiza by area, 28,000 residents covering the entire south of the island: Es Vedrà (the 382 m vertical limestone monolith offshore from Cala d'Hort, with its 'third most magnetic place on Earth' lore), Sa Talaia (the island's 475 m highest peak, 2 h round-trip hike from the village), the 18th-century Església de Sant Josep in the casco antiguo plaza, the Parque Natural de Ses Salines d'Eivissa i Formentera (UNESCO Biosphere with salt pans, flamingos and Posidonia seagrass meadow), and the Sa Pedrera (Atlantis) quarry-cove descent. Beaches from Cala d'Hort, Cala Vadella, Cala Tarida, Cala Molí and Cala Carbó on the south-west to Cala Jondal, Sa Caleta, Es Codolar and the 2.7 km Platja d'en Bossa club strip on the south. Ibiza Airport (IBZ) sits inside the municipality 2 km from Platja d'en Bossa; TIB buses L24/L21/L25/L26 cover the area, no rail or ferry port, Aquabus seasonal coastal boats for summer cove-hopping, Es Vedrà boat tours from Cala d'Hort.

name: Santa Eulària des Riu
intro: Calmer family resort on Ibiza's east coast (38,000 year-round residents), wrapped around the whitewashed 16th-century church-fortress of Puig de Missa, the Riu de Santa Eulària (the only year-round river in the Pitiüses) with its Pont Vell Roman bridge and mil de baix windmill, a long Paseo Marítimo and Marina, and the Saturday Las Dalias hippie market in Sant Carles. Year-round dog beach at Cala Nova (north of Es Canar), shoulder-season tolerance at Cala Llonga and Cala Pada, and Ibiza Airport (IBZ) 22 km south-west by taxi or TIB L18 bus.

name: Santander
intro: Cantabria's bayside capital pairs the Belle Époque crescent of El Sardinero and the royal Magdalena peninsula with a year-round Brittany Ferries link to Plymouth and Portsmouth, a dedicated off-leash zone at Parque de las Llamas and a 24/7 veterinary hospital on Avenida de los Castros, the most practical Cantabrian Sea city for a dog-inclusive trip.

name: Santiago de Compostela
intro: Galicia's UNESCO-listed pilgrim capital with granite-paved squares around the cathedral, six designated off-leash dog spaces, a 24/7 reference vet hospital at Costa Vella, and a municipal 'Santiguau' programme formally listing pet-friendly venues across the old town.

name: Santorini
intro: Santorini (Thira, ~15k year-round residents, 76 km² Cycladic volcanic island) is a crescent-shaped caldera with the whitewashed cliff-top villages of Fira (capital), Firostefani, Imerovigli and Oia draped along the 300 m caldera rim. The 10 km clifftop caldera path from Fira to Oia is the signature dog walk (dawn or after 17:00, paws burn at midday), the hilltop villages of Pyrgos and Megalochori offer calmer Cycladic atmosphere away from the summer crush, and the Akrotiri Bronze Age Minoan site under its bioclimatic roof is the headline archaeology. Beaches are volcanic: Red Beach (Akrotiri), 7 km Black Beach Perissa/Perivolos, Vlychada under lunar bluffs, the boat-access White Beach. JTR airport sits 6 km southeast of Fira (year-round Aegean/SKY Express to Athens, summer EU charters), Athinios port runs Blue Star and Sea Jets ferries from Piraeus (5-8h) plus inter-island catamarans. Not a budget pet destination: hotels charge 20-40 EUR/night pet supplement, July-August sees 50k+ daily tourists and asphalt hits 50-60 °C. Apr-May and October are the dog-friendly windows.

name: Sanxenxo
intro: Sanxenxo is Galicia's premier Rías Baixas beach resort in Pontevedra, known for the 750 m Praia de Silgar, the long Silgar-Baltar seafront promenade and easy day trips to Combarro and the O Grove peninsula. Leashed dogs are welcome on its promenades and off-season beaches, and the nearest year-round dog beaches lie about 20 km away at O Grove.

name: Saranda
intro: Saranda is the sun-soaked gateway to the Albanian Riviera, a fast-emerging coastal city looking across the strait to the Greek island of Corfu. With its palm-lined promenade, the UNESCO ruins of Butrint nearby, and beaches that turn quiet and leash-free in the off-season, it is a rewarding, affordable dog-friendly escape.

name: Scheveningen
intro: Scheveningen is The Hague's North Sea beach resort, with a long boulevard, iconic Pier, protected dunes and year-round dog beaches at either end of the coast.

name: Sète
intro: Sète is a 44 000-resident Hérault port city built on the slopes of Mont Saint-Clair between the Mediterranean and the Étang de Thau oyster lagoon, nicknamed the Venice of Languedoc for its working canal grid. Highlights include the 175 m Mont Saint-Clair panoramic terrace, the Cimetière Marin where Paul Valéry rests, the 12 km Plage de la Corniche with the year-round off-leash Lazaret plage canine, and the dog-friendly Sète-Mèze ferry across the Étang de Thau to the Bouzigues oyster villages.

name: Setúbal
intro: Setúbal is a working Atlantic port wrapped around the Sado estuary, with translucent Arrábida coves 15 minutes from the centre, a year-round dolphin ferry to the Tróia peninsula, the 110 km² Serra da Arrábida Natural Park rising directly from the sea, and an underrated tasca culture built around choco frito and Moscatel. 24/7 vet cover and an easy 50-minute Fertagus train to central Lisbon anchor every itinerary.

name: Seville
intro: Seville's orange-tree lined streets, riverside promenades, and vibrant terrace culture make it one of Andalusia's most dog-friendly cities.

name: Sibenik
intro: Sibenik is a thousand-year-old Dalmatian stone city built around the UNESCO Cathedral of St James and crowned by four hilltop fortresses. With a dog-friendly old town, the Riva waterfront and the waterfalls of Krka National Park nearby, it makes a rewarding summer base for travellers with pets.

name: Siena
intro: Siena is a 53 000-resident UNESCO World Heritage hilltop city in southern Tuscany, built around the shell-shaped Piazza del Campo and divided into 17 contrade (medieval neighborhoods) that compete in the Palio horse race on 2 July and 16 August. The white-and-black marble striped Duomo Cathedral, the 14th-century Palazzo Pubblico, the 102 m Torre del Mangia, the Fortezza Medicea panoramic ramparts, the Orto de' Pecci medieval valley garden and the Via Francigena pilgrim route through Porta Camollia and Porta Romana anchor the walled centre. Trenitalia regional Florence-Siena (1h15-1h45) accepts muzzled dogs, Tiemme/Sena buses link San Gimignano, Volterra, Montepulciano and the Crete Senesi rolling hills, and Florence FLR airport is 70 km north via direct 90 min Autostradale coach.

name: Sintra
intro: Sintra, the UNESCO Cultural Landscape 30 minutes from Lisbon, combines polychrome Romantic palaces in the Serra de Sintra, the botanical gardens of Pena, Regaleira and Monserrate, kilometres of leashy laurel-forest trails, the dramatic Atlantic cliffs of Cabo da Roca and a mild oceanic climate that stays pet-friendly year-round.

name: Sirmione
intro: Sirmione is a postcard peninsula reaching into the warm southern end of Lake Garda, crowned by a moated medieval castle and ringed by Roman ruins, thermal spas and dog-friendly rocky lake beaches. With several beaches where leashed dogs may swim, a car-free old town and dogs welcome on the lake ferries, it is one of the most rewarding pet-friendly summer bases on Lake Garda.

name: Sitges
intro: Sitges is a 30,000-resident Catalan seaside town 35 km south-west of Barcelona, with 17 beaches stretched over 3.5 km of the Costa del Garraf, a designated dog beach at Platja de la Bassa Rodona during the August-September window, the traditionally tolerant Platja dels Balmins cove, the cliff-top Església de Sant Bartomeu i Santa Tecla baroque silhouette, the Casc Antic cobbles around the Palau Maricel and Museu del Cau Ferrat, the Parc de Terramar gardens, the Parc Natural del Garraf hinterland, and a 24/7 reference vet hospital on Ctra. de Pruelles. Rodalies R2 Sud from Barcelona-Sants reaches Sitges in 35 minutes, Mon-Bus runs a 30-minute shuttle from Barcelona-El Prat (BCN) airport, and the city anchors one of Europe`s most settled LGBT travel scenes around Carnaval (February), Bears Sitges Week (September) and the Fantastic Film Festival (October).

name: Sliema
intro: Sliema is Malta's breezy seafront resort town, where a kilometres-long promenade links Tigne Point to the bays of St Julian's past the rocky Exiles foreshore. With dog-tolerant terraces, a designated dog beach and a short ferry to Valletta, it is one of the island's easiest bases for travelling with a dog.

name: Sofia
intro: Sofia is one of the EU's most affordable capitals: nearly 500 dog-friendly venues, two 24/7 emergency vet hospitals, and the 2,290 m Vitosha mountain rising directly from the city, all reachable on foot or one metro ride.

name: Sóller
intro: Sóller is a 14k orange-valley town in Mallorca's UNESCO Serra de Tramuntana, reached from Palma by the 1912 wooden Ferrocarril and from the natural horseshoe Port de Sóller by the 1913 open-air Tranvía vintage tram. Modernist Plaça d'Espanya, the GR-221 Ruta de Pedra en Sec dry-stone trail, the Pinos boat to Sa Calobra, Cap Gros lighthouse views, and naranjas + oli Sóller PDO make it Mallorca's most genuinely pet-friendly mountain base.

name: Sopot
intro: Sopot, the spa-resort heart of Poland's Tricity (between Gdansk and Gdynia), 35 000 residents, Europe's longest wooden pier (512 m) open to leashed dogs, year-round beach access for dogs since the 2025 rule change with a signposted dog stretch at entrances 43-45, twelve free off-leash runs including the agility-equipped Blonia Sopockie, and the Lesna Opera forest trails starting 15 minutes from the pier.

name: Sorrento
intro: Sorrento is a 16 000-resident Campania cliff town in the Metropolitan City of Naples and the gateway hub for the Amalfi Coast, Capri, Ischia and Pompeii, hosting roughly 3 million tourists a year. The historic Piazza Tasso anchors the centro storico, the panoramic Villa Comunale gardens look 80 m down onto the Marina Grande old fishing port, the Marina Piccola ferry terminal runs 30+ daily SNAV/Caremar/NLG hydrofoils to Capri (25 min), Ischia (50 min) and Naples (35 min), the EAV Circumvesuviana uniquely accepts muzzled dogs free of charge for the direct 35 min trip to Pompei Scavi, and the SITA SUD Amalfi Coast bus links Positano (50 min), Amalfi (1h30) and the Path of the Gods trailhead at Bomerano.

name: Spa
intro: Spa is the small Ardennes thermal town in Belgium's Liège province that gave the English language the very word "spa", and today a UNESCO Great Spas of Europe member of around 10,000 residents ringed by forest. Its compact centre gathers the Pouhon Pierre-le-Grand spring pavilion, the covered galleries of the Parc de Sept Heures, and the hillside Thermes de Spa reached by a panoramic funicular (dogs not admitted inside the baths). Just above town the vast Hautes Fagnes nature reserve unrolls roughly 700 km of marked trails where leashed dogs are welcome, while the Lac de Warfaaz offers an easy lakeside loop a short drive from the centre. The legendary Spa-Francorchamps Formula 1 circuit lies a few kilometres away for a day-trip. Trains reach Spa via Verviers on the Liège line, and the cool, wet uplands climate makes spring through autumn the most comfortable window for walking with a dog.

name: Split
intro: Split's Adriatic setting delivers the perfect combination for pet owners: a gorgeous coastline, a compact walkable old town, and an increasingly pet-friendly hospitality scene. The seaside Riva promenade and the green Marjan Hill forest park: essentially a dog-walker's paradise: are both within a short stroll.

name: St Ives
intro: A white-sand Cornish harbour town where dogs share the coast path, the seal boat trips and the harbour pubs year-round. The beach dog rules are seasonal and beach-by-beach: Porthmeor and Porthminster ban dogs 10am-6pm from 15 May to 30 September, while Bamaluz Beach and Smeaton's Pier north side stay dog-friendly all year.

name: St. Moritz
intro: St. Moritz is the alpine luxury benchmark of Graubünden's Engadin valley at 1856 m, where leashed dogs walk the frozen Lej da San Murezzan loop past the Cresta Run, ride the 1907 Muottas Muragl funicular to 2453 m for the Senda Filosofica panorama, climb the Diavolezza cable car to 2978 m above the Morteratsch glacier, and travel the UNESCO Rhaetian Railway on the Glacier and Bernina Express trains under 322 sun days a year.

name: Stavanger
intro: Stavanger, Norway's third city and the gateway to the Lysefjord, combines a UNESCO-rated wooden Old Town (Gamle Stavanger), exceptionally dog-friendly transport (free buses, free trains, free fjord ferries), the iconic Pulpit Rock 50 min east, and 35 km of dog-friendly Atlantic sand 15 min south.

name: Stockholm
intro: Stockholm's archipelago setting, vast green spaces, and dog-welcoming culture make it one of Scandinavia's best cities for pet travel.

name: Stuttgart
intro: Stuttgart sits in a green basin ringed by vineyards and beech forests, a southern German capital where Biergärten and Wirtschaften universally welcome dogs, the Schlossgarten ribbon links the centre to the Neckar, and the Bärensee forest reservoirs offer cool summer walks twenty minutes from the centre.

name: Sydney
intro: Sydney is one of the world's most dog-friendly cities, with harbour dog beaches, huge off-leash parks, and a year-round outdoor dining culture.

name: Sylt
intro: Sylt is Germany's premier North Sea beach island, a 40-kilometre ribbon of dunes, red cliffs and endless sand off the North Frisian coast, and one of the most genuinely dog-friendly destinations in the country. Every resort, from the main town of Westerland to Kampen, Wenningstedt, Rantum, Hörnum and List, has an officially designated dog beach (Hundestrand), with off-leash running on most beaches from November to mid-March. Add the purple heath of the Braderuper Heide, the glowing Rotes Kliff, the UNESCO Wadden Sea, and a car-train crossing where dogs travel free, and Sylt becomes a rare beach island built for travelling with a dog.

name: Syracuse
intro: Syracuse is a sun-drenched Sicilian city built around Ortigia, the tiny island old town of honey-coloured baroque streets, the legendary Fonte Aretusa spring and a magnificent seafront Lungomare. Just inland the vast Neapolis archaeological park preserves a Greek theatre and Roman amphitheatre, making it one of the Mediterranean's most rewarding, walkable destinations to explore with a dog.

name: Tallinn
intro: Tallinn's beautifully preserved medieval old town, coastal paths, and dog-friendly hotels make it a hidden gem for pet travel in Northern Europe.

name: Tampere
intro: Tampere, Finland's third city and the unofficial sauna capital, combines a compact lake-bordered centre, exceptionally dog-friendly transport (free trams, free trains), 22 fenced koira-aitaus, two lake dog beaches and direct rail access from Helsinki in 1h30.

name: Taormina
intro: Taormina, the cliff-top Sicilian balcony 200 m above the Ionian Sea facing Mount Etna and the location of HBO`s The White Lotus Season 2, pairs the 3rd-century BC Greco-Roman Teatro Antico with the pedestrianised Corso Umberto, the tidal-causeway Isola Bella nature reserve, the Funivia cable car down to Mazzarò beach, and the long sandy designated dog beach at Letojanni 5 km north. Trenitalia regional trains from Stazione Taormina-Giardini connect Catania CTA airport in 1 hour and Messina in 50 minutes.

name: Tarifa
intro: Tarifa, the southernmost point of mainland Europe on the Strait of Gibraltar, is a tiny medieval town that doubles as the kitesurf and windsurf capital of the world. Ten kilometres of flat-sand Playa de Los Lances open to leashed dogs out of season, the Roman ruins of Baelo Claudia behind dog-friendly Bolonia beach, a 35-minute FRS ferry to Tangier, and a 24-hour vet on-call line make it one of southern Spain`s most distinctive small-town bases for pet travel.

name: Tarragona
intro: Tarragona, Catalonia's UNESCO-listed Roman seaport on the Costa Daurada, pairs an open-air 2nd-century amphitheatre with three designated dog beaches (Platja Llarga, Platja del Miracle and Bon Caponet), the wild pine-forest cove of Cala Fonda, and 24/7 referral vet care 5 km away at AniCura Bofarull. Renfe Rodalies trains carry leashed dogs to Barcelona in 70 minutes.

name: Tavira
intro: Tavira, the quieter eastern Algarve town split by the Rio Gilão and its seven-arch Ponte Romana, opens onto the Parque Natural da Ria Formosa, the year-round Ilha de Tavira ferry from Quatro Águas (5-min crossing), the Praia do Barril mini-train and anchor cemetery, the Cabanas de Tavira sandbar, and the Cacela Velha clifftop village. The CP Linha do Algarve and Vamus EVA coastal buses run east to the Vila Real de Santo António ferry crossing the Rio Guadiana to Ayamonte in Spain.

name: Tbilisi
intro: Tbilisi is the ancient Georgian capital on the Kura river gorge, where 4th-century fortress ruins overlook sulphur bath domes and modernist glass bridges. Dogs walk off-leash in Vake Park's 148 hectares, dine on every restaurant terrace, and explore a city that ranks among the most welcoming in the world for travelling with a dog.

name: Tenby
intro: A medieval walled harbour town on the south Pembrokeshire coast, wrapped around three beaches and looking out to the monastic Caldey Island. Dogs travel free on the West Wales Line train into town and free on the Caldey boats, and the Pembrokeshire Coast Path leaves Tenby in both directions open to dogs year-round. Seasonal beach dog rules apply from 1 May to 30 September, with North Beach closed to dogs and the quiet Penally end of South Beach staying dog-friendly all year, so there is always sand and clifftop to walk.

name: Tenerife
intro: Tenerife is a year-round dog island where mild 20-26°C weather lets you walk the Costa Adeje seafront paseo in January as easily as July, with the golden-sand Playa del Cabezo dog beach in El Médano and the laurel forests of Anaga waiting inland. From the volcanic moonscape of Teide National Park to palm-lined promenades from Los Cristianos to Puerto de la Cruz, leashed dogs are welcome almost everywhere outdoors.

name: Texel
intro: Texel is the Netherlands' most painlessly dog-friendly Wadden island: a 24 km long North Sea spit 20 minutes by TESO ferry from Den Helder (dogs cross free), with five year-round off-leash dog beaches (Paal 8 Mokbaai, Paal 9 Den Hoorn, Paal 17 De Koog, Paal 28 and Paal 31 at the Eierland lighthouse), the 4,300-hectare Nationaal Park Duinen van Texel running almost the full western dune belt, and the 850-hectare De Dennen pine forest in the centre with year-round off-leash loops. Seven villages share the island culture (Den Burg as the cobbled capital, De Koog beside the dog beach pavilions, Oudeschild with the working fishing harbour and the Texelse Bierbrouwerij, Den Hoorn around its 1,500-resident square, De Cocksdorp at the lighthouse, plus Oosterend and De Waal). The De Slufter salt marsh and Wagejot mudflats on the east coast are NATURA 2000 reserves (eastern Wadden Sea coast closed to dogs year-round for bird protection). Texelhopper buses serve every village and dune entry, dogs ride free. From Schiphol Airport the door-to-ferry trip is about 1h45 by car.

name: The Hague
intro: The Hague pairs Dutch political grandeur with a 11-kilometre North Sea coastline, off-leash dunes a tram ride from the centre, and dog-friendly cafés on every corner of the Statenkwartier and Scheveningen Haven.

name: Tokyo
intro: Tokyo pairs neon Shibuya crossings and centuries-old temples with a real (if stricter) pet-travel scene: Japanese rules mean dogs ride JR and metro trains only inside carriers within set dimensions, and many venues welcome pets on terraces or in dedicated dog cafes rather than in indoor dining rooms. Registered dog runs at Yoyogi and Komazawa, Tokyo Bay seaside parks such as Jonanjima, and 24-hour English-speaking veterinary hospitals make the city genuinely workable for prepared owners who plan around the rules.

name: Toledo
intro: Toledo, the medieval Imperial City and former Visigoth, Moorish and Christian capital, is a UNESCO-rated open-air museum where Christian, Jewish and Islamic heritage meet on a single granite outcrop above the Tagus, with Madrid 33 minutes away by Avant high-speed rail.

name: Toronto
intro: Toronto is one of the rare North American cities where a dog of any size rides the subway, the streetcar and the bus free of charge, as long as you travel outside weekday rush hours. Add more than eighty designated off-leash areas, a year-round dog beach at Cherry Beach, an Ontario law that puts dogs on restaurant patios and an airport train that takes leashed dogs from Pearson to downtown, and a car-free city break with a large dog becomes genuinely workable.

name: Torun
intro: Torun is the UNESCO Old Town of brick Gothic and the birthplace of Nicolaus Copernicus, a flat medieval city on the Vistula where the entire historic core is walkable on a leash. The Rynek Staromiejski with its monumental Gothic Town Hall, the Leaning Tower (Krzywa Wieza) on the medieval walls, and the riverside Bulwar Filadelfijski all welcome leashed dogs year-round, while indoor museums (Copernicus House, Gingerbread Museum) admit assistance dogs only. MZK Torun trams and buses accept dogs on leash with the owner, around twenty fenced off-leash dog zones (wybiegi) are scattered across the city, and the cafe terraces around the two market squares welcome leashed dogs without fuss.

name: Tossa de Mar
intro: Tossa de Mar is a 5,700-resident Costa Brava sud beach town wrapped around the 12th-century Vila Vella, the only fortified medieval centre that survives on the entire Catalan coast, with four watchtowers, full battlemented ramparts and the Gothic ruins of the Sant Vicenç castle church inside. The 380 m sand Platja Gran sits beneath the Vila Vella, with smaller Mar Menuda just north-east and the secluded southern coves (Cala Bona, Cala Pola, Cala Llevadó, Cala Giverola) reachable via the 9 km Camí de Ronda GR-92 coastal path that links Tossa to Lloret de Mar. The 1917 Far de Tossa lighthouse crowns the easternmost tip, and the bronze statue of Ava Gardner on the Vila Vella rocks commemorates the 1951 filming of `Pandora and the Flying Dutchman`. There is no train station; access is by Moventis bus from Girona (1 h via Lloret) or by car on the GI-682 coast road or AP-7 motorway. Two village vets refer overnight emergencies to Centre Veterinari Can Vet in Lloret de Mar 12 km south.

name: Toulon
intro: Toulon stands out among large French Mediterranean cities for the dog-friendliness of its infrastructure: a dedicated cani-plage at Anse Tabarly with a dog swim ramp, two fenced cani-parcs on the Mourillon, the rare French municipal bus and bateau-bus network that admits large dogs on lead, and a Mont Faron cable car that takes dogs free to the 584-metre ridge.

name: Toulouse
intro: La Ville Rose on the Garonne offers dog owners green riverside parks with dedicated canitracks, an excellent emergency vet infrastructure, and the vast Bouconne forest on its doorstep, though note that Tisséo public transport bans dogs except in closed carriers.

name: Tours
intro: Tours is the Loire Valley's most pet-friendly base - half-timbered Vieux-Tours, tram and bus open to dogs of all sizes, and four major chateaux (Villandry, Chenonceau, Amboise, Chambord) all welcoming leashed dogs in their gardens.

name: Trapani
intro: Trapani is a sun-baked western Sicilian port wrapped around a sickle of land that juts into the sea, famous for its shimmering salt pans and windmills and its hydrofoils to the Egadi islands. With a walkable old town, a breezy seafront and a cable car up to medieval Erice, it is a relaxed, dog-friendly base for a Sicilian summer.

name: Trento
intro: The capital of Trentino is an Alpine-Italian crossroads that treats dogs as part of city life: fenced dog areas with fountains in every big park since 1997, a cable car to Sardagna that welcomes dogs for 1.20 euros, frescoed Renaissance squares to stroll on leash, dog beaches on Lake Caldonazzo 25 minutes away and the cool trails of Monte Bondone at 1,500-2,100 m when the valley heats up.

name: Treviso
intro: Venice without the crowds, 30 minutes from the lagoon by train: canals and frescoed arcades explored entirely outdoors, the flat Restera towpath along the Sile river, a municipal network of fenced dog runs, two 24/7 veterinary hospitals, and the UNESCO Prosecco hills starting 20 minutes north.

name: Trieste
intro: Trieste, Friuli-Venezia Giulia's Habsburg port capital, blends Adriatic seafront, Viennese cafés and Karst plateau hikes, with 22,000 registered dogs, official off-leash areas and Bau Beach swimming at Barcola making it one of north-east Italy's most pet-friendly bases.

name: Trogir
intro: Trogir is a tiny UNESCO-listed Venetian town on a walled island off the Dalmatian coast near Split, all marble lanes, a Romanesque cathedral and a palm-lined Riva. With dog-friendly konoba terraces, nearby Ciovo dog beaches and Split Airport just 6 km away, it makes an easy, scenic summer base for travellers with a dog.

name: Tromso
intro: Tromso, the Arctic capital 350 km north of the Arctic Circle, is the gateway to the Northern Lights and the Midnight Sun. Mild summer highs of 14 C suit brachycephalic and senior dogs, the Fjellheisen cable car climbs to a 421 m city panorama, and the Norwegian leash law (1 April-20 August) protects nesting wildlife.

name: Trondheim
intro: Trondheim, Norway's third city and the medieval capital, combines the UNESCO Nidaros Cathedral (the world's northernmost Gothic cathedral), the colourful Bakklandet wooden quarter, dog-friendly transport (free buses, free trains, the world's northernmost tramway), and 80 km² of Bymarka urban forest.

name: Turin
intro: Italy's northern baroque capital, 18 km of covered porticoes, 35+ fenced dog areas, a 10 km Po riverside walk and the Alps an hour away. One of Italy's most weather-sheltered dog-friendly cities.

name: Uppsala
intro: Uppsala is Sweden's most relaxed dog-travel city after Stockholm - a compact medieval university town with a 108-hectare urban forest, seven municipal hundrastgårdar, a designated river dog beach and a fika culture that welcomes dogs at the café table.

name: Utrecht
intro: Utrecht is one of the Netherlands' most reliably dog-friendly cities, compact medieval centre, free dogs on city buses and trams, multiple off-leash parks, and a canal-cruise operator that welcomes dogs at no charge.

name: Valbona
intro: Valbona is a glacial valley in the Albanian Alps at 800–1,200 m altitude, surrounded by peaks exceeding 2,500 m. One of the most remote accessible valleys in the Balkans, it offers pristine river swimming, leash-free hiking through Valbona Valley National Park, and the iconic crossing to Theth, all with dogs unconditionally welcome.

name: Valencia
intro: Valencia's sunny climate, Turia river park, and dog-welcoming beaches make it a superb year-round destination for pet travel.

name: Valldemossa
intro: Valldemossa is a 2,000-resident village perched in the UNESCO Serra de Tramuntana 17 km north of Palma, defined by the 14th-century Real Cartuja monastery where Chopin and George Sand wintered in 1838-39 (cell 4), the cobbled lanes and flower-lined balconies of the casc antic, the Plaça pública and Església Parroquial de Sant Bartomeu, the Casa Natal de Santa Catalina Tomàs (Mallorca's only Catholic saint, born here 1531), the Mirador des Pi des Català and Mirador de Valldemossa Tramuntana views, the GR-221 Ruta de Pedra en Sec dry-stone trail passing through the village, the twisty road down to Cala Valldemossa and the Port de Valldemossa fishing port, and coca de patata Valldemossa as the signature local pastry.

name: Valletta
intro: Valletta's limestone fortress city, Grand Harbour bastions, and pet-friendly ferry network make Malta's UNESCO capital a year-round Mediterranean destination for dog owners.

name: Vancouver
intro: Vancouver is one of North America's most dog-friendly cities, wrapped by ocean, mountains and rainforest, where the outdoors is the whole point. Leashed dogs are welcome along the roughly 9-kilometre Stanley Park seawall and on more than thirty Park Board off-leash areas, from the fenced grounds at Trout Lake to the forest trails of Pacific Spirit, while a short official list of dog beaches (Spanish Banks, Sunset Beach, Hadden Park) opens up mostly in the cooler months. The catch is transit: TransLink only allows dogs on the SkyTrain, buses and SeaBus inside a small carrier on your lap, so a larger dog gets around on foot, by car, by dog-accepting taxi, or on the leashed-dog-friendly Aquabus ferries. Patios rule the food scene, 24/7 emergency vets like Canada West have the city covered, and Capilano Suspension Bridge is a rare marquee attraction that lets leashed dogs cross.

name: Vannes
intro: Vannes, the gateway to the Gulf of Morbihan, preserves three-quarters of its 13th-to-16th-century fortified walls around a fully pedestrian half-timbered Vieille Ville, with the 15 000 m² Jardin des Remparts, the 27 000 m² Parc de la Garenne, the BreizhGo Bateaux Bus du Golfe ferries to the car-free Île d'Arz and Île aux Moines, and the Conleau peninsula seaside walk, making it one of Brittany's most rewarding pet-friendly bases.

name: Venice
intro: Venice is surprisingly dog-friendly: dogs travel on the vaporetto, explore quiet campi, and are welcomed in many trattorias.

name: Verona
intro: Verona is a UNESCO-listed romantic city with an Arena, a legendary Juliet balcony, and a welcoming attitude to dogs in its wine bars, parks, and alfresco terraces.

name: Vichy
intro: The Queen of France's spa towns walks beautifully with a dog on the leash: the Art Nouveau covered galleries of the Parc des Sources give shade, the English-style Parc Napoleon III opens onto a 6 km lakeside loop around the Allier, and the Source des Celestins pavilion pours free sparkling water. Dogs stay outdoors though, the thermal spa, the opera and the lake beaches are all off-limits.

name: Vienna
intro: Vienna's grand parks, dog-friendly cafés, and highly-rated hotels make it a top destination for pet owners in Central Europe.

name: Vigo
intro: Galicia's biggest port city on a deep Atlantic fjord, with 18 official off-leash dog areas, a 24/7 reference vet hospital, and the Castro park citadel with sunset views over the Cíes Islands (pet entry strictly banned on the islands themselves).

name: Villach
intro: A 62,000-resident Carinthian river city on the Drava with a Renaissance Hauptplatz, two warm Alpine lakes within 10 km (Faaker See and Ossiacher See), the Dobratsch nature park and a working 24/7 vet. Italian and Slovenian borders are 30-40 minutes away.

name: Villefranche-sur-Mer
intro: Villefranche-sur-Mer is a 5,000-resident Côte d'Azur harbour town between Nice and Monaco, built into a steep ochre amphitheatre above one of the deepest natural harbours in the western Mediterranean. Headlines include the working Port de la Santé quays, the 13th-century covered Rue Obscure, the 16th-century Citadelle Saint-Elme (Musée Volti + chapels), the Chapelle Saint-Pierre des Pêcheurs frescoed by Jean Cocteau in 1957, the 1 km Plage des Marinières (the longest beach on the Côte d'Azur) and the neighbouring Cap Ferrat 10 km Sentier du Littoral around Pointe Saint-Hospice and Plage de Passable. The Gare SNCF de Villefranche-sur-Mer sits on the TER Marseille–Vintimille line (6 minutes from Nice-Ville, 15 from Monaco); Lignes d'Azur bus 100 runs Nice–Menton every 15 minutes, the Ligne 80 climbs onto Cap Ferrat. The nearest airport is Nice Côte d'Azur (NCE), 15 minutes by car or TER. Beach access for dogs runs October to end-April; harbour terrace dining is reliable nearly year-round.

name: Vilnius
intro: Vilnius is the EU's greenest capital and one of its most affordable: a UNESCO Old Town walkable in a day, free pets on every bus, two 24/7 emergency vets, and nearly 500 dog-friendly venues listed on the national pet directory.

name: Vitoria-Gasteiz
intro: Capital of the Basque Autonomous Community on the Álava plateau, European Green Capital 2012, with the 30 km Anillo Verde green belt encircling the city (Salburua wetlands with deer and storks, Olarizu botanical garden, Zabalgana cork-oak forest, Armentia oak woods, Zadorra river park). The almond-shaped Casco Medieval hilltop holds the Gothic Cathedral of Santa María and Plaza de la Virgen Blanca; 256k inhabitants, the most extensive dog-walkable urban green network in Spain.

name: Warsaw
intro: Warsaw has transformed into one of Central Europe's most dynamic capitals, and its hotels have kept pace: many now welcome pets with open arms. The Łazienki Royal Park, with its sprawling grounds and peacocks, makes a dream off-lead destination for visiting dogs.

name: Whitby
intro: A historic North Yorkshire fishing port where the ruined abbey crowns the East Cliff, the swing bridge splits the old town, and dogs are welcome almost everywhere outdoors. Trains on the Esk Valley Line take dogs free, the cliff paths and 199 Steps are made for walking, and nearby Runswick Bay and Sandsend give year-round dog beaches around the seasonal town ban.

name: Windermere
intro: England's largest lake in the heart of the Lake District, where dogs are welcome on almost every fell and footpath, from the short Orrest Head climb to the National Trust lakeshore at Fell Foot. Trains, local buses and the lake cruises all take dogs free, and British pub culture makes Bowness genuinely easy with a dog.

name: Woolacombe
intro: A North Devon surf village on a magnificent three-mile Blue Flag beach, where dogs share the seafront, the National Trust headlands and the year-round dog stretch of sand. The beach dog rules are zoned and seasonal: the busy north end of Woolacombe Sands is closed to dogs from Good Friday or 1 April to 30 September, while everything south of Mill Rock, down to Putsborough, stays dog-friendly off-lead all year (North Devon Council PSPO, fines up to 100 pounds). There is no railway station, so most visitors arrive via Barnstaple and the Stagecoach 303 bus.

name: Wroclaw
intro: Wroclaw is one of Poland's most genuinely dog-loving cities. The Rynek (one of the largest medieval market squares in Europe) is ringed by café terraces that welcome dogs without fuss, while the Odra river and its many islands offer kilometres of riverside paths that connect Park Szczytnicki and the Cathedral Island into one giant urban dog walk. Public transport is free for animals, around forty fenced off-leash zones are scattered across the city, and the famously friendly local bronze dwarfs add a daily scavenger hunt your dog will happily share.

name: Yokohama
intro: Yokohama turns Japan's stricter pet-travel culture into an easy win by concentrating its best dog spots along one compact, walkable bayfront. Leashed dogs share the Minato Mirai promenades, historic Yamashita Park and the open-air Marine & Walk and Red Brick Warehouse, while a large natural-grass dog run on Rinko Park gives real off-leash space minutes from the station. Trains and buses take dogs only inside a carrier, and a dedicated night emergency hospital near Yokohama Station backs up the many small-animal clinics, so a prepared owner who plans around the rules finds the port city genuinely dog-friendly.

name: York
intro: York, England's walled medieval gem on the Ouse, combines a 5 km dog-friendly city walls circuit, the photogenic Shambles, and unconditional pub welcome with day-trip access to North Yorkshire dog beaches via direct LNER trains.

name: Zadar
intro: Zadar is the Dalmatian coast's most under-rated city - Roman forum, pre-Romanesque Saint Donatus rotunda, the wave-powered Sea Organ and the LED Greeting to the Sun, all on a compact dog-friendly peninsula.

name: Zagreb
intro: Zagreb is one of central Europe's most relaxed capitals for travelling with a dog, a flat, walkable city of Habsburg-era squares, a 316-hectare lakeside park, dog-friendly café terraces on Tkalčićeva, and the world's shortest public funicular linking the medieval Upper Town.

name: Zahara de los Atunes
intro: Zahara de los Atunes is a whitewashed Atlantic fishing village on the Costa de la Luz, wrapped around the Castillo de las Almadrabas and one of Andalusia's longest wild beaches. With dune boardwalks toward Atlanterra and the Cabo de Plata cliff, it is built for long, slow summer stays with a dog.

name: Zakynthos
intro: Zakynthos pairs the Venetian squares of Zakynthos Town and the pine-clad Bochali castle hill with quiet olive-grove walks across the Vasilikos peninsula and dramatic west-coast viewpoints. For dog owners it is a relaxed, outdoors-first Ionian island, where the real planning is around summer heat and the strict loggerhead-turtle protections in Laganas Bay.

name: Zandvoort
intro: Zandvoort is Amsterdam's North Sea beach town, a short direct train from the city and Haarlem, with a wide sandy strand, dune reserves and seasonal dog-beach rules.

name: Zaragoza
intro: Aragon's capital, Spain's fifth-largest city (675,000 people) anchored by the Basílica del Pilar on the Ebro river, with 126 designated off-leash zones (one of the largest networks of any Spanish city), the 27-hectare Parque Grande Labordeta, and AniCura Emvet 24/7 referral hospital.

name: Zell am See
intro: Lake, glacier and summit with the dog in tow: Zell am See lets muzzled, leashed dogs ride the Schmittenhohe cable cars, the Kitzsteinhorn glacier lifts and even the Lake Zell boats, while the Erlberg dog zone and the Klammsee give them room to run and swim. Just pack the muzzle, it is the key that opens the whole region.

name: Zermatt
intro: Zermatt is the car-free Alpine resort village at the foot of the Matterhorn, a 5,800-resident icon where dogs ride the Sunnegga funicular and the Gornergrat railway, swim at the Leisee dog beach, and walk the legendary Five Lakes route past the Stellisee reflection.

name: Zurich
intro: Zurich has some of Europe's highest standards for pet welfare: dogs ride trams, enter shops, and are welcomed in many top hotels.

name: Cinque Terre
intro: The Cinque Terre are five UNESCO-listed fishing villages strung along the Ligurian cliffs, and they are surprisingly dog-friendly where it counts: leashed dogs ride the regional train and the ferry, and walk the coastal CAI trails and the reopened Via dell'Amore. The villages are steep and their beaches restricted, so this is a destination for the paths and the sea rather than the sand.

name: Portofino
intro: Portofino is the iconic fishing village of the Italian Riviera, a cluster of pastel houses around a tiny, exclusive harbour on a steep, wooded promontory. With a dog it is honest work: there is essentially no dog beach and the coast is rocky and pricey, but the flat harbour piazzetta, the walk up to Castello Brown and the lighthouse, and the leashed trails through the Parco di Portofino to San Fruttuoso are genuinely dog-friendly, and the ferries and buses from Santa Margherita take dogs.

name: Portorož
intro: Portorož, Slovenia's Belle Époque spa resort on the Istrian coast, pairs a palm-lined seafront promenade and grand thalasso hotels with a genuinely dog-friendly hinterland, from Monty's Dog Beach at Lucija, the country's first designated dog beach, to the Forma Viva sculpture park on the green Seča peninsula, the Sečovlje salt pans and the car-free stone town of Piran next door.

name: Positano
intro: Positano is the vertical jewel of the Amalfi Coast, a cascade of pastel houses tumbling down the cliff to the sea. It is honest work with a dog: the town is a staircase of hundreds of steps, most beaches restrict dogs and summer stone bakes, but leashed dogs ride the SITA buses and the ferries and, above all, walk the spectacular Path of the Gods.
